description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary opacities.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal chest radiograph showing the thoracic cavity. There are bilateral pulmonary opacities, more pronounced in the lower lung fields, suggestive of a possible infectious or inflammatory process. The cardiac silhouette appears within normal limits, and no obvious pleural effusion is visible. The bony structures, including the ribs and clavicles, appear intact.

description.short_caption: Axial chest CT showing a cavitary lesion in the right lung.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates a cavitary lesion in the right lung. The lesion appears to have thickened walls and is surrounded by areas of consolidation. The mediastinum and heart are visible in the midline, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The image is likely obtained without contrast, as no vascular enhancement is evident.
visible_findings: cavitary lesion in the right lung

Case_10011/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Hematoxylin-Eosin stain of pericardial fluid, cell-block.

description.short_caption: Hematoxylin-Eosin stain of pericardial fluid showing inflammatory cells.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Hematoxylin-Eosin stained preparation of pericardial fluid. Multiple cells are visible, including clusters of darkly stained nuclei suggestive of inflammatory cells. The background appears relatively clear, with scattered cellular elements. The staining highlights nuclear and cytoplasmic details, aiding in the identification of cellular components.

description.short_caption: Papanicolaou stain of pericardial fluid showing cellular elements.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Papanicolaou-stained smear of pericardial fluid. The smear contains numerous cells with varying sizes and shapes. The nuclei are prominent and stained dark purple, while the cytoplasm appears lighter with a bluish hue. The arrangement and morphology of the cells suggest a diagnostic evaluation for possible infection, malignancy, or other pathological processes.
visible_findings: variation in cell size and shape

description.detailed_description: This is an echocardiographic image in a four-chamber view. The heart chambers are visible, with a hypoechoic (dark) area surrounding the heart, consistent with a pericardial effusion. The effusion is labeled with arrows, and the image includes an ECG tracing at the bottom for timing reference. The pericardial effusion appears to be moderate in size.
visible_findings: hypoechoic area surrounding the heart indicating pericardial effusion

description.short_caption: Immunohistochemical stain highlighting Human Herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8) positive cells.
description.detailed_description: This image shows an immunohistochemical stain for Human Herpesvirus-8 (HHV-8). The brown-stained cells indicate HHV-8 positivity, while the blue counterstain highlights the nuclei of other cells. The distribution of positive cells appears scattered across the field. The staining technique is specific for identifying HHV-8-infected cells in tissue or cytological samples.
visible_findings: blue counterstained nuclei of other cells

description.short_caption: Electrocardiogram showing rhythm and electrical activity of the heart.
description.detailed_description: This is a standard 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) tracing. The image displays multiple leads (e.g., I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF, V1-V6) capturing the electrical activity of the heart. The tracing shows regular intervals and waveforms, including P waves, QRS complexes, and T waves. Specific abnormalities, if present, would require further analysis of the waveform morphology, intervals, and axis.
visible_findings: P waves, QRS complexes, and T waves visible
Standard lead labeling (I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF, V1-V6)

Case_10011/figure8.jpg.source_caption: In situ hybridization for Epstein Barr virus RNA.

description.short_caption: In situ hybridization for Epstein-Barr virus RNA showing positive staining cells.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a microscopic field with multiple cells stained using in situ hybridization for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) RNA. The positive cells exhibit dark purple staining, indicating the presence of EBV RNA. The background is lightly stained, and the contrast highlights the positive cells. This technique is used to detect EBV in tissue samples.
visible_findings: dark purple-stained cells indicating EBV RNA presence

description.short_caption: Axial chest CT showing bilateral pulmonary nodules.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest demonstrates bilateral pulmonary nodules, some of which are peripherally located. The lung parenchyma appears otherwise unremarkable, with no evidence of significant consolidation or pleural effusion. The mediastinum and heart are centrally located and appear normal in this slice. No obvious lymphadenopathy is visible.
visible_findings: normal lung parenchyma aside from nodules
normal mediastinum and heart in this slice
